# Verdict: REJECT ## Overall Assessment This tooltip component implements approximately 20% of the WAI-ARIA APG Tooltip pattern. The `role="tooltip"` is present, but the entire interaction model for keyboard users and screen reader users is absent. Keyboard users cannot trigger the tooltip at all (complete access loss), and screen reader users cannot hear the tooltip content even if it were visible (no `aria-describedby` association). The conditional rendering approach also creates a structural problem where `aria-describedby` would reference a non-existent DOM id. ## Pre-commitment Predictions Before reading the code, I predicted for a tooltip component: 1. **Keyboard focus/blur handlers missing** — tooltip only responds to mouse events → **CONFIRMED** 2. **No aria-describedby association** between trigger and tooltip → **CONFIRMED** 3. **No id on the tooltip** for reference → **CONFIRMED** 4. **No Escape key dismissal** → **CONFIRMED** 5. **Conditional rendering breaks aria-describedby references** → **CONFIRMED** All five predictions were validated. No surprises — the component is a mouse-only tooltip with a single ARIA role bolted on. --- ## Critical Findings (Blocks Access) ### 1. Keyboard users cannot trigger the tooltip — complete access loss **Evidence:** `BuggyTooltip.jsx` lines 8–11 — the button only has `onMouseEnter` and `onMouseLeave` handlers. No `onFocus`, `onBlur`, or `onKeyDown` handlers exist. **User group impacted:** Keyboard-only users (complete access loss), screen reader users (cannot trigger or hear tooltip) **WCAG/APG citation:** WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) — all functionality must be operable via keyboard. WAI-ARIA APG Tooltip pattern: "The tooltip is shown when the element is hovered **or focused**." **Why this matters:** A keyboard-only user tabs to the button and receives no additional information. The tooltip content is permanently inaccessible. There is no workaround — the information simply does not exist in the DOM for keyboard users. **Fix:** ```jsx
{content}
``` **Confidence:** HIGH --- ### 3. Conditional rendering breaks aria-describedby reference integrity **Evidence:** `BuggyTooltip.jsx` line 13 — `{showTooltip && (
)}` — the tooltip element is completely removed from the DOM when hidden. **User group impacted:** Screen reader users, all users relying on ARIA relationships **WCAG/APG citation:** WCAG 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value) — ARIA references must resolve to existing elements. WAI-ARIA APG Tooltip pattern implies the tooltip element persists in the DOM and is shown/hidden via CSS. **Why this matters:** If `aria-describedby="tooltip-content-id"` is added to the button (as the fix above suggests), it will reference an `id` that does not exist in the DOM when the tooltip is hidden. This is an invalid ARIA reference. Screen readers may log errors, and the association is broken 99% of the time (whenever the tooltip is not visible). The APG-recommended pattern keeps the tooltip in the DOM and toggles visibility via CSS (`visibility: hidden` / `visibility: visible`), so the `id` always exists and `aria-describedby` always resolves. **Fix:** ```jsx // Keep tooltip in DOM, toggle visibility via CSS
{content}
``` ```css .tooltip-content { visibility: hidden; opacity: 0; transition: opacity 150ms ease; } .tooltip-content.tooltip-visible { visibility: visible; opacity: 1; } ``` **Confidence:** HIGH --- ## Major Findings (Significantly Degrades Experience) ### 4. No Escape key dismissal **Evidence:** `BuggyTooltip.jsx` — no `onKeyDown` handler exists anywhere in the component. **User group impacted:** Keyboard-only users (if keyboard triggering is added), screen reader users **WCAG/APG citation:** WCAG 2.1.2 (No Keyboard Trap) — while a tooltip isn't a trap, the APG Tooltip pattern and general UI convention expect Escape to dismiss transient UI. WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) — all functionality operable via keyboard. **Why this matters:** Once keyboard triggering is implemented (fix for finding #1), a user who tabs to the button will see the tooltip appear. They need a way to dismiss it without moving focus away. Escape is the universal dismissal key. Without it, the tooltip persists until blur, which may be confusing. **Fix:** ```jsx onKeyDown={(e) => { if (e.key === 'Escape') { setShowTooltip(false); } }} ``` **Confidence:** HIGH --- ### 5. No aria-hidden on tooltip when not shown (if using CSS visibility approach) **Evidence:** `BuggyTooltip.jsx` line 15 — the tooltip div has no `aria-hidden` attribute. If the fix for finding #3 (keep in DOM, toggle CSS) is applied, the tooltip content will remain in the accessibility tree even when visually hidden. **User group impacted:** Screen reader users — will encounter tooltip content in reading order even when it's not visually relevant **WCAG/APG citation:** WCAG 1.3.1 (Info and Relationships) — hidden content should not be exposed to assistive technology. WCAG 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value). **Why this matters:** If the tooltip is kept in the DOM (as recommended in fix #3) but only hidden via CSS `visibility: hidden`, some screen readers may still announce the content during linear reading. Adding `aria-hidden="true"` when not shown ensures the content is excluded from the accessibility tree until it's relevant. **Fix:** ```jsx
``` **Confidence:** MEDIUM (depends on whether `visibility: hidden` is used — if `display: none` is used, the element is already removed from the a11y tree, but then aria-describedby breaks again) --- ## Minor Findings (Friction but Workaround Exists) ### 6. No unique id generation for multiple tooltip instances **Evidence:** The component accepts `trigger` and `content` as props but generates no unique `id`. If multiple `BuggyTooltip` instances render on the same page, they will all use the same `id="tooltip-content-id"`, causing `aria-describedby` to reference the wrong tooltip. **WCAG/APG citation:** WCAG 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value) — ARIA references must be unique and resolve correctly. **Fix:** Use `React.useId()` (React 18+) or a `useRef` with a counter to generate unique ids: ```jsx const id = useId(); // Then: aria-describedby={id} and id={id} ``` **Confidence:** HIGH (will become a real bug the moment a second instance is rendered) --- ## Enhancements (Best Practice Not Met) ### 7. No `aria-expanded` or state indicator on trigger While the APG Tooltip pattern does not require `aria-expanded` (unlike disclosure patterns), adding a subtle indicator (e.g., an info icon with `aria-hidden="true"`) would signal to all users that additional information is available. This is a UX enhancement, not a WCAG requirement. ### 8. No `prefers-reduced-motion` consideration If a fade-in transition is added (as suggested in fix #3), it should respect `prefers-reduced-motion`: ```css @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .tooltip-content { transition: none; } } ``` WCAG 2.3.3 (Animation from Interactions) — Level AAA, but good practice. --- ## What's Missing (Gaps) | Gap | Impact | |-----|--------| | `onFocus` / `onBlur` handlers | Keyboard users cannot trigger tooltip (CRITICAL) | | `aria-describedby` on button | Screen readers cannot associate tooltip with trigger (CRITICAL) | | `id` on tooltip element | `aria-describedby` has nothing to reference (CRITICAL) | | `onKeyDown` for Escape | No keyboard dismissal path (MAJOR) | | Persistent DOM presence of tooltip | `aria-describedby` references non-existent id when hidden (MAJOR) | | `aria-hidden` toggle | Hidden tooltip content may leak into a11y tree (MAJOR) | | Unique id generation | Multiple instances will collide (MINOR) | | `useId()` or equivalent | Framework-idiomatic unique id (ENHANCEMENT) | --- ## Multi-Perspective Notes | Perspective | Alarm Level | Trigger Signal | |-------------|-------------|----------------| | Screen reader | **HIGH** | No aria-describedby, no id, conditional rendering breaks references | | Keyboard-only | **HIGH** | No onFocus/onBlur, no Escape handling — complete access loss | | Low vision | **MEDIUM** | Cannot trigger tooltip; if visible, no contrast data provided | | Cognitive | **MEDIUM** | Information only available on hover — undiscoverable; no persistent access | | Vestibular & motion | **LOW** | No animations in current code; would apply if transitions added | | Auditory access | **LOW** | No media elements | | Environmental contrast | **LOW** | No CSS provided to evaluate; no color-only indicators in markup | ### Screen reader user experience: Tabs to the button. Hears: "Button, [trigger text]." No indication that additional information exists. No way to discover or hear the tooltip content. The `role="tooltip"` on a conditionally-rendered div is invisible to the user because it's not in the DOM and not referenced by any ARIA relationship. **Complete information loss.** ### Keyboard-only user experience: Tabs to the button. Nothing happens. The tooltip never appears. There is no keyboard path to trigger it, no keyboard path to dismiss it, no keyboard path to access the content. **Complete access loss.** ### Low vision user experience: Same as keyboard — cannot trigger the tooltip. If they use a screen reader (common at 200%+ zoom), same as screen reader user. If they rely on visual hover, the tooltip may appear but there's no contrast data to verify legibility. ### Cognitive user experience: The tooltip content is only available on a transient hover interaction. A user who doesn't know to hover over the button will never see the information. There's no persistent, discoverable way to access the tooltip content. The interaction model is inconsistent with other UI patterns where information is always available. --- ## Verdict Justification **REJECT** — This component has two CRITICAL findings that represent complete access loss for entire user categories (keyboard-only users cannot trigger the tooltip; screen reader users cannot hear it). These are not edge cases or minor friction — the core purpose of the component (displaying supplementary information) is entirely unavailable to these users. The component has one correct element (`role="tooltip"`) but is missing the entire interaction model that makes the pattern functional. This is the textbook "80% ARIA pattern" anti-pattern — actually worse, it's 20%. The role is present but the association, keyboard handling, and state communication are all absent. **Path to ACCEPT:** 1. Add `onFocus`/`onBlur` handlers (fixes keyboard triggering) 2. Add `id` to tooltip + `aria-describedby` to button (fixes SR association) 3. Switch from conditional rendering to CSS visibility toggle (fixes reference integrity) 4. Add `onKeyDown` for Escape (fixes dismissal) 5. Add `aria-hidden` toggle (fixes a11y tree leakage) 6. Use `useId()` for unique ids (fixes multi-instance collision) All six fixes are straightforward and can be implemented in under 30 minutes. The component should not ship in its current state. --- ## Open Questions (Unscored) 1. **Is this component used in a context where the tooltip content is also available elsewhere?** If the same information is available in a persistent location (e.g., a help panel), the severity of the keyboard/SR findings drops from CRITICAL to MAJOR (workaround exists). If the tooltip is the *only* source of this information, the findings stand as CRITICAL. 2. **Is there a parent component that wraps this in a `role="group"` or provides additional context?** If the parent provides `aria-describedby` or a label that includes the tooltip content, the association gap is partially mitigated. 3. **What is the intended tooltip duration?** If the tooltip is meant to be a brief hover hint (like a native `title` attribute), the severity is lower. If it contains critical information (e.g., form field explanations, error details), the severity is higher. The current code suggests it's meant to be a persistent-on-hover tooltip, which raises the stakes. --- ## A11y Evidence Finding (Structured) ``` finding_id: tooltip-no-keyboard-trigger fingerprint: a3f7c2e1 source: BuggyTooltip.jsx:8-11 (onMouseEnter/onMouseLeave only, no onFocus/onBlur) wcag_or_apg: WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard; WAI-ARIA APG Tooltip pattern section_508_fpc_context: WCAG 2.0 Level A (2.1.1) — in scope for Revised Section 508 severity: CRITICAL perspective_alarms: keyboard=HIGH, screen-reader=HIGH evidence: Button element has onMouseEnter and onMouseLeave props only. No onFocus, onBlur, or onKeyDown handlers present in source. reproduction_steps: 1. Render BuggyTooltip. 2. Tab to the button. 3. Observe: tooltip does not appear. expected_behavior: Per APG Tooltip pattern, tooltip appears on focus of trigger element. actual_behavior: Tooltip only appears on mouse hover. Keyboard focus produces no visual or programmatic change. trend: new ``` ``` finding_id: tooltip-no-aria-describedby fingerprint: b8d4e9f2 source: BuggyTooltip.jsx:8 (button has no aria-describedby), BuggyTooltip.jsx:15 (tooltip has no id) wcag_or_apg: WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value; WAI-ARIA APG Tooltip pattern section_508_fpc_context: WCAG 2.0 Level A (4.1.2) — in scope for Revised Section 508 severity: CRITICAL perspective_alarms: screen-reader=HIGH evidence: Button element has no aria-describedby attribute. Tooltip div has role="tooltip" but no id attribute. No ARIA relationship exists between trigger and tooltip. reproduction_steps: 1. Render BuggyTooltip. 2. Hover to show tooltip. 3. Inspect DOM: button has no aria-describedby. 4. Screen reader announces button with no reference to tooltip content. expected_behavior: Per APG Tooltip pattern, trigger element has aria-describedby pointing to tooltip's id. Screen reader announces tooltip content when reading the trigger. actual_behavior: No ARIA relationship. Screen reader announces only the button's text content. Tooltip content is inaccessibly orphaned. trend: new ```
